text:
alicia: Heads-up — Savings Plan GPU coverage for prod fleet dropped to ~58% over the last 7d. Renewal for the current purchases is in 12 days. Looks like most uncovered usage is `g5.xlarge` and `p4d` in us-east-1.
ben: Ugh. Does that 58% include lab/dev accounts or is that strictly prod?
alicia: It's aggregated across org (prod + dev + staging). If you filter to tags `env:prod` it's ~71%, dev/staging are dragging it down.
nina: Do we have a breakdown by region? My jobs are mostly in eu-west-1 and I want to know if my team will be affected.
raj: Quick snapshot I ran: us-east-1 = 62% utilized, eu-west-1 = 85%, us-west-2 = 49%. Bulk of unreserved consumption is burst/short-lived training infra spawns in us-west-2.
sre-bot: Reservation report summary: total_sp_commitments=6400USD/month, active_instances_covered=42, uncovered_hours=1124h (7d window). Missing SKUs: g5.xlarge (40%), p4d.24xlarge (35%), g5.12xlarge (25%).
ben: OK. Two angles: (1) we can tighten allocation in us-west-2 and push non-critical jobs to spot/ephemeral pools; (2) for renewals, consider a mix of regional convertible SPs + shorter commitment for p4d.
alicia: Agree. Also note Dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated customers) are pinned and cannot use our cloud SPs — that also affects utilization math. I flagged that in the spreadsheet.
nina: For my team — we can gate training runs behind `--allow-spot` and bump retry limits. Will push a PR to the infra policy.
raj: Ben, can you run the 30-day utilization query and create a coverage heatmap by SKU+region? Need to see which SKUs are consistently used vs bursty. A CSV would be ideal.
ben: On it. I'll run `aws ce get-reservation-utilization --time-period Start=2026-03-01,End=2026-03-31 --granularity=DAILY` then aggregate by `instanceFamily` and `region`.
ben: Early numbers show p4d usage is very spiky — high peak but low sustained hours. That argues against long-term 3yr standard commitments for p4d unless we consolidate.
alicia: If we can't consolidate p4d, consider 1yr convertible or lean on Savings Plans for compute with flexible instance family mapping. Also check if any reserved instances are convertible and can be exchanged.
ina: Can we also look at scheduling bigger experiments to eu-west-1 where we have higher coverage? That might lower marginal cost.
raj: Network/regional constraints: some datasets are in us-west-2 S3 buckets (GDPR sensitive). Moving them to eu requires approvals. Not trivial.
ben: Action items: 1) I'll publish a SKU-region heatmap by EOD tomorrow. 2) Alicia + Raj to list embedded customers/dedicated pools that affect coverage. 3) Nina to PR spot-fallback gating. 4) We meet Thurs to decide on renewal mix.
alicia: Also considering short-term: buy 3-6 month convertible reservations for the highest-util SKUs in us-east-1 to avoid rate increases while we finalize plan. Thoughts?
ben: That could work as a bridge. But check marketplace liquidity before buying standard RIs — selling our excess later needs a market.
ina: 👍 will reduce noncritical runs in us-west-2 starting tonight.
raj: I'll add a column in the spreadsheet for migration friction (data residency, egress cost).
sre-bot: Reminder: Renewal window opens in 10d. Current auto-renew flag = false.
alicia: Turning auto-renew off was intentional. We want to decide mix manually.
ben: Cool. I'll upload the heatmap CSV to #eng-infra-reports and tag the ticket in zenhub.
alicia: Thanks all. If anyone spots big one-off projects that will spike GPU hours next week tag them here — we may want to temporarily pause or cover with on-demand.
ben: ping me if you want a quick model of cost vs coverage for 1yr vs 3yr vs SP — I can run scenarios.
ina: noted.
raj: Leaving notes in the infra-runbook about pausing new large GPU allocations until we have the renewal plan.
alicia: End.
